title: Evidence & Claims Standard | What JPNentry will and will not claim
description: How JPNentry treats testimonials, case studies, diagnostic scores, supplier claims and business-result statements.
content:
Trust is damaged when marketing language is stronger than the evidence behind it. JPNentry aims to separate verified facts, estimates, internal diagnostic judgments and future targets.
Testimonials and endorsements
JPNentry should not publish a customer or partner testimonial as an endorsement unless the statement and attribution are genuine and the use is permitted.
Case studies
A case study should distinguish what actually happened from what was proposed or expected. Confidential commercial information should not be disclosed without permission.
Supplier and stock claims
A supplier website, marketplace listing or third-party statement is not automatically treated as verified stock. Confirmation level should be stated where material.
AI Visibility scores
Any JPNentry AI Visibility score is an internal prioritization framework. It is not an official metric issued by OpenAI, Google, Microsoft or another AI/search provider.
Sales and ranking claims
JPNentry does not claim that a diagnostic or optimization recommendation guarantees rankings, leads, bookings, revenue or inclusion in an AI answer.
Commercial estimates
Freight, exchange-rate, lead-time and landed-cost estimates should be labeled as indicative until the relevant provider or supplier confirms them.
Current versus historical evidence
Where information can change materially, the relevant date or validity basis should be stated instead of presenting an old figure as current.
When evidence is incomplete
The preferred response is to say what remains unconfirmed and what must be checked next.

title: JPNentry Outreach & Contact Standard
description: How JPNentry handles outbound business outreach, duplicate prevention, relevance, opt-outs and contact preferences.
content:
JPNentry uses targeted B2B outreach to identify potential buyers, suppliers, travel partners and service customers. This page states the standard we aim to follow.
Public business contacts
Outbound contact should use a public business contact, an existing business thread or another legitimate B2B contact route. Personal or private contact information should not be invented or guessed.
Relevance before volume
A company should be contacted because there is a reasonable connection between its visible business activity and the specific JPNentry offer or request.
One company, one active campaign touch
For a defined campaign, JPNentry aims to avoid sending the same offer repeatedly to multiple addresses at the same organization.
Existing threads are preferred
When a legitimate prior business conversation exists, a relevant follow-up should remain in that thread rather than create unnecessary duplicate threads.
Do-not-contact
A clear opt-out, complaint or do-not-contact request takes priority over future sales activity. The submitted address should be suppressed from further outbound sales contact.
Duplicate or irrelevant outreach
Recipients can report duplicate or irrelevant outreach through the Contact Preferences form.
No forced engagement
Many JPNentry sales messages explicitly state that no reply is necessary when the offer is not relevant.
No bypassing platform safety limits
If an email provider or connected service blocks or limits a send, JPNentry should not attempt to evade that safety control through another channel merely to force delivery.

title: How to Read a JPNentry Quote | Price basis, lead time and limitations
description: A plain-language guide to understanding JPNentry sourcing quotations and commercial checkpoints.
content:
A sourcing quote is useful only when the commercial basis is clear. This guide explains the terms JPNentry may use when presenting a Japan-side sourcing option.
Unit price
The quoted unit price should be read together with its currency, quantity basis and validity. A low-quantity supplier price may not apply to a large-volume requirement.
Ex-Warehouse / EXW-style basis
The goods price is presented at the Japan-side source or warehouse before the buyer's international freight, destination charges, duties and taxes unless otherwise stated.
FCA / FOB / CIF and other delivery bases
If a quotation uses a transport-related basis, the included and excluded charges should be stated. Do not assume customs duty, import tax or destination handling is included unless written.
Confirmed stock versus orderable quantity
Confirmed stock means the relevant source has indicated the quantity is currently available. Orderable quantity may depend on manufacturer supply, accumulation over time or later confirmation.
Lead time
Lead time may be supplier-confirmed or estimated. If it is estimated, JPNentry should not present it as a guaranteed delivery date.
Price reconfirmation
Manufacturer pricing, exchange rates and freight rates can change. If a price is subject to reconfirmation at order time, that condition should be stated.
Quote validity
A quote may have a validity period because stock, supplier pricing and transport conditions can change.
Commercial no-go
If the landed cost, minimum quantity, specification or timing makes the transaction commercially unrealistic, JPNentry may stop the quotation process instead of presenting a misleading offer.
Before you pay
If anything in a quote is unclear, ask for clarification or verify the communication through the Trust Center before paying.

title: Transaction Readiness Checklist | Before you buy, quote or supply
description: A practical checklist for buyers and suppliers before a JPNentry sourcing or coordination transaction moves forward.
content:
A transaction should become more specific as it moves closer to payment. This checklist shows the minimum commercial information JPNentry expects to clarify before a serious commitment.
Buyer checklist
• Exact item / service / specification
• Required quantity or participant count
• Acceptable condition or substitution rules
• Destination and required timing
• Target price or commercial threshold where available
• Delivery / Incoterm preference if relevant
• Regulatory, qualification or documentation requirements
• Who has authority to approve the order
Supplier / operator checklist
• Exact item / service being offered
• Genuine/OEM/aftermarket/used/refreshed condition clearly stated
• Confirmed quantity versus orderable / estimated quantity
• Unit price, currency and price basis
• Lead time and quote validity
• Payment terms
• Cancellation / return / warranty basis where relevant
• Export, transport or qualification limitations
JPNentry checkpoint before payment
Before requesting or recommending a commercial payment, JPNentry aims to have the key item/service, quantity, price basis, payment structure and material limitations documented in writing.
If any material point is still an estimate rather than confirmed, that distinction should be visible.
